item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Quiet Caption Over The Lake

turns.text: Put “A little room to breathe” over this photo, near the bottom in clean white lettering. Keep the whole wide photo, just add the caption.

item.tests: Tests exact caption rendering, readable placement, and preservation of the supplied photograph.

answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: A little room to breathe — English, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Style and placement: Clean white lettering near the bottom; calm and understated.
answer_sheet.Picture and output size: Use lake.jpg, retain the full 16:9 frame; free-tier image size is fine.

must_haves: The caption reads exactly 'A little room to breathe', without quotation marks.
The caption is white, readable, and placed near the bottom with no clipped letters.
The supplied mountain lake, pine trees, and sky remain recognizable and retain the original full framing.
The caption appears as a graphic overlay, not as a physical object in the scene.

turns.text: Put “A little room to breathe” over this photo, near the bottom in clean white lettering. Keep the whole wide photo, just add the caption.
turns.agent:
I couldn't add the caption. Magic Hour turned down the edit because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was made and no credits were used.

I'd already used the cheapest image editing option on the Free plan: about 5 credits for one image at 640px. Every other option costs at least that much, so trying a different one wouldn't get around the problem.

**The edit I tried to run:**
- **Caption:** "A little room to breathe", exactly as you wrote it
- **Placement:** centered near the bottom, over the lake, in clean white lettering
- **Rest of the photo:** the full wide frame, uncropped and otherwise unchanged

**To get this done, you could:**
1. **Add credits to your Magic Hour account** (top up or wait for your credits to refresh). Tell me when that's done and I'll run the same edit.
2. **Add the text yourself in a free editor** like Canva, Photos or Preview. That way the photo stays exactly as it is and the spelling is guaranteed. An AI edit like this one sometimes changes the picture a little or gets a letter wrong.
